subject: Voyager request: conditional activation SLA variance for multi-region failover
messages:
From: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@voyagerpay.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@voyagerpay.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Voyager request: conditional activation SLA variance for multi-region failover

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the platform brief last week — Voyager's infra team reviewed Redwood's cold/warm standby options and we have a request on the SLA side before we proceed to procurement. Our compliance team requires a narrower activation model for cross-region failover due to data residency and runbook restrictions. Specifically: we need a documented agreement where Redwood can optionally route traffic to a single warm-standby region for up to a 48-hour window during declared incidents if instantaneous multi-region switchover would violate our internal controls.

Concretely, we are asking for a conditional activation variance that:
- Allows warm-standby activation with an RTO up to 60 minutes and RPO up to 15 minutes (instead of the standard 15m/5m profile we expect from dedicated customers) for a controlled period following an incident declaration.
- Limits the variance to declared incidents only and requires a post-incident runbook review and confirmation within 72 hours.
- Includes explicit fallback obligations and a reporting cadence for the activation window.

We recognize this is non-standard and may have availability and cost implications for Redwood. To help accelerate, I've attached Voyager_Security_Questionnaire.pdf and the compliance team's high-level acceptance criteria. Marta from our security group is on copy and can clarify the controls.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a documented carve-out or an SLA addendum and an estimate for any pricing uplift? We'd like to get a draft agreement before our legal team kicks off procurement next week.

Best,
Tom Erickson
Head of Infrastructure, Voyager Pay

Attachment: Voyager_Security_Questionnaire.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@voyagerpay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@voyagerpay.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Voyager request: conditional activation SLA variance for multi-region failover

Tom —

Thanks for the clear note and the questionnaire. We can work with you on a bounded variance but will need to align on operational controls, monitoring, and liability language. High level thoughts:

- From an operational standpoint we can support a conditional warm-standby activation with a longer RTO/RPO for a limited, documented window. That will depend on the activation trigger and whether Voyager wants automatic routing or a manual runbook-triggered switchover.
- We'll need to define exact telemetry that confirms an incident (synthetic failures, region health metrics, post-mortem thresholds).
- There are cost and availability trade-offs — maintaining higher KV-cache priming and extended reserved burst capacity during the variance window will increase unit costs.

Copied Karthik (solutions) and Lauren (legal) to scope the technical fallback matrix and sketch the contractual language. Karthik — can you draft a fallback matrix with estimated RTO/RPO, expected token-cost uplift, and an activation checklist? Lauren — can your team propose a narrow SLA addendum that limits exposure (timebox, incident-only, reporting obligations)?

I'll assemble a mutual action plan and aim to get a draft SLA addendum over by EOD tomorrow. If useful, let's set a 30-min call with Voyager security to walk the questionnaire.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-variance-request-summary.txt (text/plain)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@voyagerpay.com>
Cc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@voyagerpay.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Voyager request: conditional activation SLA variance for multi-region failover

Priya / Tom —

I've sketched a fallback matrix and rough cost delta (attached) — summary below:

Planned variance profile (incident-only, manual-declare workflow):
- Activation trigger: customer runbook declaration OR Redwood automated threshold (mutually agreed).
- Warm-standby activation: target RTO = 60 minutes, target RPO = 15 minutes. This assumes warm replicas with periodic KV cache priming (every 30 minutes) and a cold-to-warm ramp for some shards.
- Fallback obligations: Redwood will return to standard multi-region steering within 48 hours of incident resolution unless extended by mutual written agreement.

Availability/impact:
- During variance window, service-level availability objective will be adjusted to 96.5% for the affected logical service (we'll add explicit scope about which endpoints are covered). This is lower than the standard 99.9% but is constrained to the declared variance window.
- Estimated token-cost uplift: +18–26% while caches are primed and reserved burst capacity is provisioned. Exact numbers depend on request pattern.

Operational controls we require from Voyager:
1) Single point of contact for incident declaration and runbook confirmation.
2) Acceptance of Redwood's post-activation audit within 72 hours.
3) Read access (read-only dashboards) to the activation metrics during the window.

I've attached redwood-fallback-matrix.xlsx with technical assumptions and a sample activation checklist. Happy to walk through on a short call.

—Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-fallback-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@voyagerpay.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@voyagerpay.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Voyager request: conditional activation SLA variance for multi-region failover

Tom —

Thanks for the ask and Karthik for the technical sketch. On the contract side, Redwood is willing to consider a narrowly scoped SLA addendum provided we can agree the following guardrails:

- Timebox the variance to declared incidents only and a maximum continuous duration of 72 hours per incident unless both parties consent in writing to an extension.
- Explicitly carve out liability for indirect damages arising from variance-window reduced availability; provide service credits limited to the affected endpoints and proportional to the reduced availability objective.
- Require a post-incident report and mutual acceptance before any repeat variance for the same root cause.

I'll prepare a draft SLA addendum (SLA-variance-draft-v1.docx) that includes a section for the exact endpoint scope, activation checklist, monitoring signals, and runbook ownership. Please review and send any redlines by EOD Wednesday so we can table the doc for your procurement cycle.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: RE: Voyager request: conditional activation SLA variance for multi-region failover

Tom —

Looping back with the draft addendum attached and the internal fallback matrix Karthik prepared. Quick summary of agreed next steps so we're aligned: 

1) Voyager to review SLA-variance-draft-v1.docx and provide redlines by EOD Wed (2027-04-21).
2) Security call to walk the questionnaire — proposed slot Thu 2027-04-22 10:00 AM ET. Marta to confirm.
3) Redwood to provide a final cost uplift estimate after Voyager flags expected traffic shape for a 48-hour activation window.
4) If both parties sign the addendum, variance will be operationalized as a manual-declare workflow with a one-time 72-hour max per incident and mandatory post-incident audit.

If that matches your expectation I'll schedule the call and open a HubSpot task (linked).

Thanks and speak soon,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
